name: Niche trend content planner: rising Google Trends searches to content ideas

parameters.content:
## Niche trend content planner
Finds the Google searches **rising in your niche**, removes the junk and turns the rest into content ideas: the likely reason it's rising, an angle, a hook, a format and what to fact-check.

### Setup (5 minutes)
1. **Apify:** open *Google Trends* and create a credential. On **n8n Cloud**, click the **sign-in button** and approve in Apify: no token to copy. On **self-hosted** n8n, set *Authentication* to **API Key** and paste your token from apify.com (Settings → API & Integrations). Install the Apify node first if n8n asks (search "Apify").
2. **AI:** open *Gemini model* and add a **Google Gemini** credential (free key at aistudio.google.com). It suggests topics and writes the ideas. Any other chat model works: swap the node. No AI? Set `useAI` to false in *Defaults* and you get the list of rising searches instead.
3. **Sheet and messages (optional):** pick your sheet in *Read keyword sheet* and *Add to Google Sheet*; turn on *Send to Slack* or *Send to Telegram*.

### Three ways to use it (labelled Way 1-3 on the canvas)
**Way 1 · Web form**: activate the workflow and open the *Form* URL, or share it with a client. Only the first question is required; ideas appear on the next page.
**Way 2 · Google Sheet, every Monday**: one row per topic (`niche`, `keyword`, optional `audience`, `country`, `formats`, `active`). A row with just a niche gets topics suggested.
**Way 3 · Test run**: edit *Test input* and click **Execute workflow**.

### Inputs → one shape
Each source has an adapter that outputs the same rows: `keyword, niche, audience, country, timeRange, formats, useAI, source`. An empty keyword means "suggest keywords for this niche"; an empty field is filled from *Defaults*. To add Airtable, Notion or a webhook, add one adapter that feeds *Defaults*.

Owner settings (AI on or off, ideas per niche, default country) live in *Defaults*, not on the form: the person filling the form only answers questions about their content.

## Way 1 · Web form
Activate the workflow, then open or share the *Form* URL. People answer a few questions and see their ideas on the next page.

## Way 2 · Google Sheet, every Monday
One row per topic in a `Keywords` tab. Ideas land in the `Ideas` tab, with a summary in Slack or Telegram.

## Way 3 · Test run
Edit *Test input*, then click **Execute workflow** to see a result right here.

### Keywords: suggested when missing
People describe a niche ("ai product roadmap") differently from how they search it ("cursor", "vibe coding"), and described phrases have almost no Google data. So when a niche has fewer than `suggestKeywordsBelow` keywords and AI is on, the AI suggests `suggestedKeywords` searchable ones: products, ingredients, tools, problems. Keywords Google has no data for cost nothing. The results list every keyword searched and mark the suggestions, so people can keep the good ones. Without AI, a niche with no keywords is searched as written, with a note asking for a few keywords.

### How ideas are picked (per niche)
Junk out (prompt-like searches and generic Breakouts from bot traffic), relevance (AI score 0–10, or word match without AI), variants merged, ranked by growth with a boost for searches rising under several keywords, spread across keywords. Weekly sheet runs never repeat an idea within 8 weeks and flag what's new. Tuning values sit at the top of *Clean and rank*.

### AI or report
With AI each niche gets one request: relevance, why rising, title, angle, hook, format and a fact-check list (*Structured Output Parser* keeps fields valid). Without AI, or if the AI call fails, the niche gets the **rising searches report**: the cleaned list with growth, variants and Google Trends links.

### Results
- **Form:** shown on the results page, with the keywords searched.
- **Sheet / test runs:** one row per idea in your sheet (status "to review", same columns for ideas and report) and a summary in Slack or Telegram (off until set up).
Nothing is published automatically.

messageValues.message: You are a search researcher. You know how ordinary people phrase Google searches in a niche, and you suggest the short, concrete terms they type, never marketing language.

parameters.jsCode:
// One AI request per niche: the model sees the whole list, so it can compare and drop the weak ones.
return $input.all().map(({ json: n }) => {
  const list = n.candidates.map(c =>
    `${c.n}. "${c.text}"${c.topicType ? ` [topic: ${c.topicType}]` : ''}: rising ${c.growth}`
    + ` under ${c.seeds.map(k => `"${k}"`).join(', ')}${c.variants.length ? `; also searched as ${c.variants.map(v => `"${v}"`).join(', ')}` : ''}`
    + `${c.echo ? ' (just my keyword again)' : ''}${c.isNew === false ? ' (was rising last time too)' : ''}`).join('\n');
  const prompt = [
    `Today is ${new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)}.`,
    `I make content about: ${n.niche}.`,
    n.audience ? `My audience: ${n.audience}.` : 'My audience: people interested in this niche.',
    `Formats I publish: ${n.formats || 'blog post, short video'}.`,
    ``,
    `These searches are rising on Google right now (${n.country || 'worldwide'}, ${n.timeRange}), with their growth and the keyword they rose under:`,
    list,
    ``,
    `For every numbered item, return:`,
    `- relevance (0-10): how good a content opportunity it is for my audience right now.`,
    `  9-10: specific and clearly for my audience: a question they ask, a product, rule, event or story they care about.`,
    `  6-8: relevant, but broader or less timely.`,
    `  3-5: a broad name on its own (a company, platform, category, or just my keyword again) that rises for too many reasons to tell what people want; or about the same story or product type as a better item in this list.`,
    `  0-2: unrelated to my niche, spam, or bot traffic.`,
    `  Judge the search itself, not the idea you could write about it: a broad name stays at 5 or less even if you can think of a good angle for it.`,
    `- whyRising: one sentence starting with "Likely" or "Possibly": the reason people may be searching it now. You only see Google search data and your knowledge may be out of date, so never state recent events, versions or prices as facts; say "Unclear" if you don't know. If the search looks like the title of a specific article, paper, book, video or news story, say so.`,
    `- title, angle (what to cover), hook (the opening line), format (one of my formats; vary them across ideas where it fits).`,
    `- checkBeforePublishing: every fact the idea relies on that must be verified before publishing: numbers, prices, dates, versions, rules, study results, and the original source when the search points to a specific article or story. Empty only when there is nothing to verify.`,
    ``,
    `Rules for title, hook and angle:`,
    `- No numbers, prices, percentages, amounts or time claims unless they are in the search itself or listed in checkBeforePublishing. Counting your own steps or tips ("3 steps") is fine.`,
    `- No personal experience ("I tested", "my results"): the creator hasn't done it yet.`,
    `- Put a year in a title only when the search is about that year.`,
    `- Each idea must be distinct. When several items are about the same story or product type, give the best one an idea that covers them all and score the others 5 or less.`,
    ``,
    `Return one entry per item, using its number as "n", and set "nicheId" to "${n.id}".`,
  ].join('\n');
  return { json: { ...n, prompt } };
});

messageValues.message: You are a practical content strategist. You write specific ideas a creator could publish this week, never generic ones. You never present a fact you aren't sure of: anything that needs checking goes in checkBeforePublishing.
